discovery_health.diagnosis: Generic topic search, targeted historical-author search and event-to-X second-hop search all failed to return verifiable current X status permalinks through the available public index route. Upstream event discovery itself worked.

cohort_definitions.recent: Publicly verifiable X observations from the current feed window; none admitted across the first two runs.
cohort_definitions.evergreen: Older evidence with explicit durable rediscovery value; none admitted in these fresh-feed runs.

confounders: No fresh verifiable X status samples are available yet, so current structural comparisons cannot be performed.
Historical repository samples are intentionally not relabeled as current evidence.
Search-engine result ranking cannot be used as a proxy for X distribution.
recent_changes: The collector now has a durable feed contract, schemas, query rotation plan and route-level yield tracking.
The first run tested topic/public X search routes and preserved zero yield.
The second run explicitly tested AUTHOR_WATCH, TOPIC_WATCH and EVENT_TWO_HOP; upstream event discovery succeeded but no verifiable X status permalink was returned.
next_sampling_priorities: Allow the scheduled collector to rotate to different authors and topic buckets instead of repeating this manual probe.
Continue EVENT_TWO_HOP using distinctive current event names, but never treat upstream event popularity as X reach evidence.
If the third consecutive run still has zero usable X status samples, mark discovery as blocked and require a visible-browser or other authorized X source rather than weakening evidence rules.
Once fresh samples exist, deliberately collect ordinary/low-distribution controls and prefer similar-author/similar-age comparisons.
note: This is discovery-health analysis, not content-pattern analysis. No viral mechanism is promoted until fresh X observations exist.
